title: This AI startup has roughly 50 employees, no product and has never published a word of research. It's worth $32 billion
excerpt: Backed by a $5 billion Nvidia investment, Ilya Sutskever's SSI has gone from launch to a $32 billion valuation in about a year.
content_html:
Most startups need a product, paying customers and a believable path to profitability before investors start throwing billions of dollars their way.

Safe Superintelligence (SSI) appears to need none of the above.

Must Read

  • Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

  • Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake — here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

  • Millionaires under 43 hold only 25% of their wealth in stocks. Here's where their money is actually going

Nvidia is reportedly investing about $5 billion in SSI, the highly secretive AI company founded by former OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever, according to Bloomberg. Alongside the investment, SSI will gain access to Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin platform, which the companies say will increase its computing capacity tenfold.

"We have research that is worthy of scaling up, and having access to a big NVIDIA computer will let us do so," Sutskever said in a press release issued by Nvidia and SSI. "We're incredibly proud to be partnering with Jensen and the NVIDIA team, and we are confident that our big bet on the Vera Rubin platform will take us to the next level."

Founded in 2024, SSI is taking what it calls a "straight shot" at building safe and aligned artificial superintelligence. That means focusing on research rather than releasing commercial products or chasing short-term revenue.

Pressure is on

Nvidia's investment in SSI is the latest sign of just how much money is pouring into artificial intelligence. Global private investment in AI reached $344.7 billion in 2025, up 127.5% from the year before, according to Stanford University's 2026 AI Index.

Within months of launching, the startup raised $1 billion at a valuation of roughly $5 billion. Seven months later, another $2 billion funding round pushed that figure to $32 billion — a 540% jump before the company had released a product or published any research.

Behind that valuation is a small team. Sutskever launched SSI with Daniel Gross, a former Apple AI executive, and Daniel Levy, a former OpenAI researcher. Gross initially oversaw fundraising and computing needs, while Sutskever and Levy led the research. Gross has since left the company.

That leaves SSI under pressure to prove it's worth the price tag. The exact terms of Nvidia's investment have not been disclosed, although the Financial Times reported that commitments of this size are often tied to a startup reaching certain milestones.

在投资者开始投入数十亿美元之前，大多数初创公司都需要产品、付费客户和可靠的盈利途径。

安全超级智能（SSI）似乎不需要上述任何一个。

必读

  • 杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 支持一个平台，让任何人都可以以低至 100 美元的价格投资出租房屋——无需真正成为房东即可像房东一样积累财富的 6 种方法

  • 43岁以下的百万富翁仅将其财富的25%投资于股票。 这就是他们的钱实际去向的地方

据彭博社报道，英伟达正在向 SSI 投资约 50 亿美元，SSI 是一家高度保密的人工智能公司，由前 OpenAI 首席科学家 Ilya Sutskever 创立。 除了投资之外，SSI还将获得Nvidia的下一代Vera Rubin平台的使用权，两家公司表示该平台将使其计算能力提高十倍。

Sutskever 在 Nvidia 和 SSI 发布的新闻稿中表示：“我们的研究值得扩大规模，使用大型 NVIDIA 计算机将使我们能够实现这一目标。” “我们非常自豪能够与 Jensen 和 NVIDIA 团队合作，并且我们相信，我们对 Vera Rubin 平台的巨大押注将使我们更上一层楼。”

SSI 成立于 2024 年，正在采取所谓的“直接行动”来构建安全且一致的人工智能。 这意味着专注于研究而不是发布商业产品或追逐短期收入。

压力已开启

Nvidia 对 SSI 的投资是人工智能领域投入大量资金的最新迹象。 斯坦福大学2026年人工智能指数显示，2025年全球人工智能私人投资达到3447亿美元，同比增长127.5%。

成立后几个月内，这家初创公司筹集了 10 亿美元，估值约为 50 亿美元。 7 个月后，另一轮 20 亿美元的融资将这一数字推至 320 亿美元——在该公司发布产品或发表任何研究之前，这一数字增长了 540%。

这一估值的背后是一个小团队。 Sutskever 与前 Apple AI 高管 Daniel Gross 和前 OpenAI 研究员 Daniel Levy 共同推出了 SSI。 格罗斯最初负责筹款和计算需求，而苏茨克弗和利维则领导了这项研究。 格罗斯此后离开了公司。

这让 SSI 面临着证明其物有所值的压力。 英伟达投资的具体条款尚未披露，尽管英国《金融时报》报道称，这种规模的投资往往与初创公司达到某些里程碑有关。
